page.title: Adapters
page.purpose: State exactly what each source of money events can and cannot currently tell us, so an operator can judge which figures elsewhere are complete.

priorities.statement: Which adapters are unavailable, why, and how old their last success is
What is therefore missing from figures on other pages
That manual and file adapters sit in the same list as API adapters
Configuration and run controls, ranked below the three above

states.description: The adapter list at rest.
Nothing in flight; the surface is at rest and its controls are usable.
A user-triggered operation is in flight and its outcome is not yet known.
An operation completed; the result is announced, not merely rendered.
First read of the surface's data; layout is reserved so nothing shifts on arrival.
A write is in flight; the affected control is disabled and says why.
A background read is refreshing data the user is already looking at.
A user-requested re-read of data already on screen.
No adapters are registered at all. Distinct from every adapter being unavailable.
Some contributing source could not be read; what is missing is named.
Displayed data is older than its freshness window; its age is shown.
Input was rejected before submission; the offending field is identified.
The request failed; the reason and the next action are stated.
An automatic retry is in progress; attempt count and next attempt are visible.
The caller's role does not permit this; what role would is stated.
The client cannot reach the API; queued or read-only behavior is explained.
An adapter ran and failed. It reports a reason and the age of its last success, and never a zero result.
A registered adapter that has never executed. Deliberately distinct from one that ran and failed — different facts, different next actions.
An adapter cannot authenticate because its credential is absent from the secret store. Named as a configuration gap, never as a data result.
Every registered adapter is available and within its freshness window — the only state in which figures elsewhere stand without a caveat.
The thirteen operator fields are present but unanswered; absent is shown as absent, never as zero.
An operator-input dry run or apply is in flight and the affected controls say why.
An operator-input apply completed and its report names written and skipped fields.
An operator-input value was rejected before apply and the field is identified.
Some operator fields are current while others remain absent; the missing paths are listed.
A supplied operator field is outside its declared window and is marked stale with its age.

elements.name: Adapters
elements.description: Every registered adapter in one list — API, file import and manual entry together, with no visual hierarchy between them.
Per-adapter disposition: available, unavailable, or never-run. Carries a text label, never colour alone.
Why an unavailable adapter failed, in the operator's terms. Inline, not behind a drill-in.
How long ago this adapter last succeeded. The figure that lets an operator judge how much of the position is missing.
What is therefore absent from figures elsewhere — the bridge between this page and the position surface.
Assertive notice that a credential is missing from the secret store, naming the adapter and the remedy. Never displays the credential or its handle.
Manual entry's row in the adapter list, carrying the same fields and prominence as any API adapter.
Guidance for registering a first adapter when none exist.

elements.name: Operator financial inputs
elements.description: The thirteen fields requested from the operator, grouped by monetary, measure, and refused-derived-rate class.

elements.name: Operator input status
elements.description: Each field's absent, current, or stale status, observed time, and reason.
Dry-run or apply report naming fields written and fields skipped with reasons.
Explains why subscriptions.mrr is derived and cannot be entered as a journal posting.

claims.statement: An unavailable adapter states why it failed and how old its last success is, without opening a detail view.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-004 verbatim. 'Unavailable' with no reason and no age gives the operator nothing to act on and nothing to judge the position by.

claims.statement: An adapter that has never run is perceivably different from one that ran and failed.
claims.rationale: The same class of distinction as a missing figure versus a zero, one level down. They have different causes and different remedies; collapsing them hides a configuration error inside an outage. The live UI distinguishes these from adapter metadata; the current route-only capture provider cannot create the two adapter histories in one validation matrix.

claims.statement: An unavailable adapter states what is consequently absent from figures on other surfaces.
claims.rationale: Priority 2. Without this, the operator must infer the blast radius of an outage, which is exactly the inference the product exists to remove.

claims.statement: A missing credential is presented as a configuration gap with a remedy, never as an empty or zero result.
claims.rationale: SECURITY.md: an adapter that cannot reach its credential must report unavailable with a reason and never fall back to an unauthenticated path or an empty result.

claims.statement: Manual entry appears in the same adapter list as API adapters, not in a separate or secondary section.
claims.rationale: OT-P0-006. Manual and file adapters are ordinary adapters by construction; the UI must not reintroduce the hierarchy the contract removed.

claims.statement: Unavailable adapters read before available ones.
claims.rationale: Priority 1. What is broken is the reason to open this page. Direction-aware so the order survives RTL.

claims.statement: Having no adapters registered is perceivably different from having adapters that are all unavailable.
claims.rationale: 'Nothing configured' and 'everything broken' are different situations with different next actions, and both render as an absence of data. The live UI renders empty guidance separately from unavailable rows; the current route-only capture provider cannot mutate the adapter registry between state captures.

claims.statement: Every adapter disposition carries a text label rather than relying on a status tint.
claims.rationale: PRD accessibility rule. Availability is the most consequential fact on this page and must survive without colour perception.

claims.statement: The operator sees all thirteen fields with status and age before entering a value, and absent is not rendered as zero.
claims.rationale: The replacement must be a trustworthy entry path, not a form that hides which source facts are missing.

claims.statement: A dry-run report names every field to write and every field skipped, and apply is a separate explicit action.
claims.rationale: The existing importer owns the three-class classification; the console exposes that report before changing the journal. The route-only capture provider cannot invoke the separate dry-run action, so this mutation-path claim is manually attested rather than machine-gated.

claims.statement: subscriptions.mrr is displayed as a refused derived rate and cannot be submitted as a posting.
claims.rationale: MRR is computed from telemetry and has no direct journal basis in this scenario.
